intended_action.name: 掌系 Z 方向平移

thumb.trace: Panel 1: broad radial thumb from the left thenar mass bends toward the sphere and ends in the nail-bearing pad at its left edge.

index.trace: Panel 1: A rounded candidate fingertip peeks above the sphere, with a candidate proximal ray visible beneath it; the sphere hides most of the connecting chain, so its unique base-to-tip identity cannot be confirmed.

middle.trace: Panel 1: the front central contact ray follows a distinct base from the distal palm, bends upward and ends in the pad contacting the sphere on its right; it is provisionally the middle by visible base order.

ring.trace: Panel 1: next ulnar ray is separate to the right of the contact finger, extends diagonally upward-right through visible joint regions and ends in the higher of the two free ulnar tips.

little.trace: Panel 1: outermost ray follows the ulnar palm edge to a shorter tip farther right and below the ring, with its own visible bends.

hands.count_observation: Four complete external rays can be followed; the sphere hides the independent index chain. A partial pad or proximal strip is not sufficient to certify a fifth digit.
hands.length_observation: The thumb, front contact finger and two open ulnar fingers have plausible visible lengths after allowing for flexion; the hidden index centerline and its relationship to the contact finger cannot be checked.
hands.joint_observation: Visible thumb and ulnar rays attach continuously and bend plausibly; the broad sphere occlusion prevents checking the index phalangeal chain and its connection behind the middle finger. Entire visible hand, wrist and forearm are framed.
